opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll; full-time employees may have up to write, and admin is not permitted since Engineer does not own Payroll. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E045 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. With basic training, maximum access is read. Requested write, so grant read.
reason: The team notes conflict on employment type: HR states full-time (max write), while Security states contractor with basic security training (max read). Under the Security record, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. With basic training, the maximum allowed level is read. Douglas requested write, which exceeds the contractor max, so the granted level is read (the conservative maximum consistent with the more restrictive verified record).
